arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the
# destination.
#
# Destination is read from the BACKUP_DEST environment variable so it can be
# set per-host by whatever schedules this job (cron env, systemd unit,
# register-job.sh, etc.) without editing this script. Two forms are
# supported:
#   - a local path (e.g. /mnt/backups or ./backups)      -> plain copy
#   - a remote scp target (e.g. user@host:/path/to/dir)  -> scp
#
# If BACKUP_DEST is not set, we fall back to a local "./backups" directory
# next to this script so the job still succeeds and produces a usable
# artifact instead of silently failing.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
LOG_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/logs"
DEFAULT_DEST="$SCRIPT_DIR/backups"

DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-$DEFAULT_DEST}"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"
BUNDLE_PATH="$SCRIPT_DIR/$BUNDLE"

if [ ! -d "$LOG_DIR" ]; then
    echo "backup.sh: log directory '$LOG_DIR' not found" >&2
    exit 1
fi

tar -czf "$BUNDLE_PATH" -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        # Remote target, e.g. user@host:/path/to/dir
        scp -q "$BUNDLE_PATH" "$DEST"
        echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"
        ;;
    *)
        # Local path/mount.
        mkdir -p "$DEST"
        cp "$BUNDLE_PATH" "$DEST/"
        echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST/$BUNDLE"
        ;;
esac

arguments.command: chmod +x backup.sh; sh -n backup.sh && echo "syntax ok"; ./backup.sh; echo "exit=$?"; ls -la; ls -la backups; rm -f logs-*.tar.gz; rm -rf backups

- Added a check that `logs/` exists, kept `set -eu` for safety, and tested it end-to-end (syntax check + actual run confirming the tarball is created and copied to the fallback local destination).
